chapter: Barnet, 52nd Street and New York recording dates
title: The benzedrine coffee record date
summary: Parker soaked a benzedrine inhaler in coffee, Rubberlegs drank it by mistake and went wild during the session.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Yeah, yes, anyway, we -- it was either real late at night or early in the morning, and we all had black coffee, about ten cups of black coffee. So in these days these benzedrine inhalers were very popular. So Charlie Parker, he didn't have any stuff this time, so he broke open a benzedrine inhaler, and this thing was equivalent to 75 benzedrine tablets, and he put it in the coffee to let it soak, you know.

And so finally Rubberlegs was already half drunk, had some bad liquor, man. He didn't drink nothing but cheap liquor. So he got to hulling, and it got hot because he -- and he wanted some coffee. So Teddy Reeg was running this date, and so big, fat Teddy Reeg -- you might see him going around with Basie a lot -- so he grabbed the coffee up, and he drank it, you know, and then he really got wild after that.
Yeah. And so later on Byrd went and got a coffee, and he drank it, you know. And he told us, he say, man, my constitution is getting terrible. This stuff

ain't even phazing me. Well, we didn't even know what had actually happened, but Rubberlegs was already drunk, and he had got ahold to it. He kept saying, this is bitter coffee, man, and, you know. So he got ahold to it, this benzedrine coffee. But we didn't know it.

And we were recording along, and, man, he's breaking out in a sweat, and he's cussing there, boy, he called everybody Miss So and So. He told Dizzy, Miss Gillespie, you keep playing those wrong notes behind me, I'm going beat your brains, and he had fists big as hams, man, this guy did. So we all was getting kind of frightened because the guy was getting so desperate, you know, wild around there.

He got after Teddy. He said, put out these lights; it's too hot in here. You know, so Teddy put out the lights. It got dark, and the only light you could see was back in the control room. So he told -- told Charlie Parker, what are you playing? They're some wrong notes. You know how Charlie play flatted fifths? He's getting after Charlie --

And so he sang one of those records. I think it's 'What's the Matter Now,' one of these things. He's going all out of tune up on the thing -- 'wha-a-t's the ma-a-atter now,' and all, and we were -- we die -- almost roll on the floor laughing, man, and this is when we found out that he had got
the -- Charlie Parker's cup by mistake, and this was the wildest record date you -- we never did get through with it -- you ever saw in your life.

And they put those things out. I heard one of them one time, and it was the funniest thing I ever heard. This guy was screaming and screeching, and it -- it was so funny. You've got to hear those records if you get a chance.

But he told somebody a couple days later that -- he said that stuff had him high for two, three days. He said he couldn't go to sleep. You know, you can't sleep with a lot of benzedrine. For two or three days he say his heart was just pounding, you know, and this -- this was Charlie's stuff, because Charlie couldn't wake up.
